provenance.canonical-source: apps/v4/registry/new-york-v4/ui/badge.tsx — ONE element, one cva with six variants, sole source for every style cell. Token values from apps/v4/app/globals.css (light block from line 100, dark from line 144). Examples read for composition and for the numeric case: apps/v4/registry/new-york-v4/examples/badge-{demo,secondary,destructive,outline}.tsx and apps/v4/examples/radix/badge-{variants,icon,link,rtl,colors}.tsx. Read only to fix the boundary (NOT canonical): apps/v4/registry/bases/{radix,base,aria}/ui/badge.tsx, which move the identical structure and the identical six-variant list behind `cn-badge-variant-*` class tokens — same conclusions, no extra capability; and apps/v4/content/docs/components/{radix,base,aria}/badge.mdx.
provenance.six-variants-not-four: badge.tsx's cva ships SIX variants — default, secondary, destructive, outline, ghost, link — with `defaultVariants: { variant: "default" }`. The docs' own badge-demo.tsx renders only the first four, and `ghost` and `link` appear only in apps/v4/examples/radix/badge-variants.tsx (ghost) and badge-link.tsx. Found by reading the cva object rather than the demo, which is why they are modelled.
provenance.hover-is-link-only: THE AXIS THIS COLUMN NEARLY LOST. Every hover declaration in badge.tsx is written with Tailwind's `[a&]:` arbitrary variant — `[a&]:hover:bg-primary/90`, `[a&]:hover:bg-accent`, `[a&]:hover:underline` — which compiles to a selector that only matches when the element is an <a>. Since the component renders a <span> unless `asChild` is passed, a default shadcn badge has NO hover response at all. Modelled as prop.interaction with a real element branch, exactly as card.template.json modelled its static/button/link fork, rather than as an unconditional hover.
provenance.primary / primary-fg: classes `bg-primary text-primary-foreground` -> --primary globals.css:107 / :150 and --primary-foreground :108 / :151. Note the INVERSION: light is near-black on near-white, dark is near-white on near-black. Contrast Salt, whose badge is mode-invariant.
provenance.danger / danger-fg / pill-bg-danger: class `bg-destructive` -> --destructive globals.css:115 / :158, with `dark:bg-destructive/60` compiling to color-mix(in oklab, var(--destructive) 60%, transparent) — so the dark destructive fill is a 60% mix rather than the raw colour. The label is `text-white`, a LITERAL Tailwind colour and not a token, identical in both modes, which is why danger-fg is declared modeInvariant. --destructive-foreground exists in globals.css and this component does not use it.
provenance.pill-bg-*-hover: classes `[a&]:hover:bg-{primary,secondary,destructive}/90`. Tailwind v4 compiles the /90 modifier to color-mix(in oklab, <color> 90%, transparent), the same derivation input.shadcn.json used for its /30 and /50 modifiers. Written out per mode rather than as an expression over another slot, so no custom property has to resolve across a mode boundary (lesson 2).
provenance.accent-bg / accent-fg: classes `[a&]:hover:bg-accent [a&]:hover:text-accent-foreground` on the outline and ghost variants -> --accent globals.css:113 / :156 and --accent-foreground :114 / :157. A DIFFERENT hover mechanism from the three filled variants' 90% self-darken, which is why style.badge.hover reads indirection slots rather than restating a formula.
provenance.border-base: class `border-border` on the outline variant -> --border globals.css:117 / :160. The 1px WIDTH comes from the cva base's bare `border` utility, which Tailwind does not tokenise (docs/foundations/border-style.md).
provenance.fg-base: class `text-foreground` on the outline variant -> --foreground globals.css:102 / :145 (pure black in this checkout).
provenance.focus / ring-alpha / ring-alpha-danger: classes `focus-visible:border-ring focus-visible:ring-[3px] focus-visible:ring-ring/50` from the cva BASE -> --ring globals.css:119 / :162, plus the destructive variant's `focus-visible:ring-destructive/20 dark:focus-visible:ring-destructive/40`. The alpha is a slot so the destructive override changes only the alpha, per mode — the same shape input.shadcn.json used for aria-invalid.
provenance.pill-radius: class `rounded-full`. Tailwind v4 renders this as calc(infinity * 1px); Tailwind is NOT vendored in this clone, so the concrete 9999px is [R] — visually identical, and the same value M3's corner-full carries. docs/foundations/shape.md already records that shadcn has no pill token of its own: 'components use rounded-full, a bare Tailwind utility'.
provenance.pill-padding / pill-gap: classes `px-2 py-0.5` and `gap-1` against Tailwind's default --spacing: 0.25rem -> 8px inline, 2px block, 4px gap.
provenance.icon-size: class `[&>svg]:size-3` = 0.75rem = 12px, paired with `[&>svg]:pointer-events-none`. Density-invariant because shadcn has no density capability at all (docs/foundations/density.md).
provenance.type-label: classes `text-xs font-medium` = 0.75rem/1rem at weight 500. Matches docs/foundations/typography.md line 58's caption/notation row for shadcn. badge.tsx sets no font-family utility, so the family is the ambient Tailwind sans stack — recorded as an ambient inheritance rather than a component token, the same honesty tooltip.shadcn.json and input.shadcn.json used.
provenance.transition-props: class `transition-[color,box-shadow]`. The property list is [S]; 150ms / cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) are Tailwind's own defaults and Tailwind is not vendored in this clone, so the timing is [R] — the identical caveat input/select/dialog/tabs.shadcn.json recorded.
provenance.no-dot-no-anchoring: CONFIRMED ABSENCE, and it is a double one. badge.tsx has no dot form and no positioning utility. The anchored dot shadcn DOES ship is `AvatarBadge`, exported from the avatar component (apps/v4/examples/*/avatar-badge.tsx imports it from ui/avatar) — a part of a different canonical component on a different docs/COMPONENTS.md row. And the NUMERIC badge in shadcn's own badge-demo.tsx is not a component capability either: it is `className="h-5 min-w-5 rounded-full px-1 font-mono tabular-nums"` applied per instance, i.e. the counter shape is consumer CSS. Recorded rather than modelled.
provenance.no-size-token: CONFIRMED ABSENCE: badge.tsx declares no height, min-height, min-width or width beyond `w-fit`, so a shadcn badge's height is entirely emergent — 2px padding + 1rem line-height + 2px padding + 2 x 1px border = 22px. Salt and M3 both pin a height; shadcn does not.
provenance.aria-invalid-scope-trim: The cva base carries `aria-invalid:border-destructive aria-invalid:ring-destructive/20 dark:aria-invalid:ring-destructive/40` — shadcn's shared focus/invalid block, pasted verbatim into a component that is never a form control. Declared out of scope rather than modelled: a badge has no validation state in any of the three systems, and there is no cross-system row to hang it on. The same class of scope trim input.shadcn.json made for its `file:` and `selection:` groups.
provenance.base-layout-into-chassis: `inline-flex items-center justify-center shrink-0 w-fit` are promoted to the template's `base` block as chassis layout, because Salt's pill declares the identical set (display: inline-flex, align-items: center, justify-content: center, flex-shrink: 0) and M3 has no layout token to contradict them. Declared rather than modelled as a row.

structure.shell.source: badge.tsx returns one <Comp data-slot="badge">; there is no wrapper element anywhere in the file

structure.label-format.source: badge.tsx spreads {...props}; the label is whatever the consumer nests. There is no value or max prop

structure.dot.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — see the no-dot-no-anchoring provenance entry. The anchored dot lives on `avatar` as AvatarBadge

structure.anchoring.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — no position, inset, absolute or translate utility in badge.tsx

structure.icon.source: cva base `gap-1 [&>svg]:pointer-events-none [&>svg]:size-3` — the component sizes and neutralises any SVG child; exercised by examples/radix/badge-icon.tsx and by badge-demo.tsx's Verified badge

prop.content.source: single-valued: there is no dot form

prop.placement.source: single-valued: there is no anchored form

prop.variant.source: badge.tsx cva variants object, listed SOURCE-DEFAULT-FIRST per `defaultVariants: { variant: "default" }`. A secondary-first or ghost-first list would have made every unqualified shadcn badge in the harness render as the wrong fill

prop.interaction.source: badge.tsx `asChild = false` is the declared default, so static is value[0]; `const Comp = asChild ? Slot.Root : "span"`. The `link` value is not cosmetic — every [a&]:hover rule in the component is unreachable without it (see the hover-is-link-only provenance entry)

prop.max.note: no value prop, so nothing to clamp

behavior.role.source: badge.tsx writes data-slot="badge", data-variant and className, and spreads the rest. No role, no aria-label, no aria-live

behavior.value-clamping.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — the label is arbitrary children; a long one is clipped by `overflow-hidden` rather than clamped

behavior.activation.source: badge.tsx binds no handler of its own; `asChild` replaces the span with the consumer's element via Slot.Root, and examples/radix/badge-link.tsx supplies <a href>. Activation is then the platform's, and the [a&]:hover styling becomes reachable at the same moment

behavior.live-region.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — no aria-live, aria-atomic or role=status

slot.label.note: including an icon: badge-demo.tsx puts <BadgeCheckIcon /> and a text node side by side

slot.icon.source: DECLARED COMPOSITION to a future icon-set component; shadcn's examples use lucide's BadgeCheckIcon and BookmarkIcon

state.rest.value: --primary fill with --primary-foreground text, INVERTING by mode
state.rest.note: near-black on near-white in light, near-white on near-black in dark

state.hover.value: link-gated; three mechanisms across six variants

state.focus.value: border-ring + a 3px ring/50 shadow, from the cva BASE
state.focus.note: declared on an element that cannot take focus unless asChild supplies a focusable one — reproduced as source has it and flagged. The destructive variant narrows the alpha to 20% light / 40% dark

style.badge.background.note: variant=default (value[0]), read through the indirection the five variant rows reassign

style.badge.size.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — see the no-size-token provenance entry; a shadcn badge is sized by its padding and line-height alone

style.badge.border-width.note: cva base `border border-transparent` — every variant carries the 1px, so switching to outline changes only a colour

style.badge.overflow.source: cva base `overflow-hidden` — a long label is clipped to the pill's full radius

style.badge.z-index.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — shadcn has no shared z-index scale (docs/foundations/layers.md) and this component sets none

style.badge.hover.source: the [a&]:hover group, expressed once over three indirection slots the variant rows reassign, so one rule carries the self-darken, the accent-pair and the underline mechanisms without restating the selector six times

style.badge.focus.source: cva base `focus-visible:border-ring focus-visible:ring-[3px] focus-visible:ring-ring/50`, drawn as a translucent box-shadow ring, the rendering input.shadcn.json established. NOTE: badge.tsx does NOT carry `outline-none`, unlike input.tsx, so the native outline is left alone and none is emitted here

style.badge.variant@destructive.source: badge.tsx `destructive: "bg-destructive text-white focus-visible:ring-destructive/20 dark:bg-destructive/60 dark:focus-visible:ring-destructive/40 [a&]:hover:bg-destructive/90"` — the only variant that touches the focus ring, and the only one whose label colour is a literal rather than a token

style.badge.variant@outline.source: badge.tsx `outline: "border-border text-foreground [a&]:hover:bg-accent [a&]:hover:text-accent-foreground"` — no bg-* class at all, so the fill falls back to the base's transparent; an outline badge is see-through, not white

style.badge.variant@ghost.source: badge.tsx `ghost: "[a&]:hover:bg-accent [a&]:hover:text-accent-foreground"` — the whole variant is its hover pair. No background, no border colour, no text colour: at rest it is a transparent box with an inherited colour, visible only once it is a link and hovered

style.badge.variant@link.source: badge.tsx `link: "text-primary underline-offset-4 [a&]:hover:underline"` — the one variant whose hover moves text-decoration rather than a colour
